chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
title: Neighborhood life and Mitchell as scout leader
summary: Harold on the neighborhood where everyone belonged to clubs; Mitchell on his Boy Scouts group and how children's respect has faded.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Seen this neighborhood here from, say, Broad Street, all these neighborhoods, musicians, price fighters, everybody belonged to the clubs and all like that. There wasn't no hanging on the corners all night long. Nine, ten o'clock at night you wouldn't see no chair and walk in the street. No, indeed. You wouldn't see no chair and walk in the street. You'd see a grand place maybe. They had to go to the drugstore coming from the club or something like that. Or the show maybe. And sometimes we used to go to the show in town, the palace or the Crescent or one of them shows like that, you know. And we'd walk home maybe sometime. We didn't feel like I'd get the street off. Yeah. It was different.

It does sound a lot different because I've been living here for four years and, you know, it's just, I'm sure completely different from the way it used to be. And when I came here all these buildings were still here and then they started tearing them down after I came here.
Yeah. Well, Rogers, how long have you been a janitor of the Santa Center?
When you came here? Oh, man, I'll tell you, I was a scout boy, you know what I mean? Yeah, I know.
You've been there as long as I can remember.

Boy scout. Oh, that's the same thing. Yeah. Because I had a group over there. Mm-hmm. Boy, I tell you, we had everything, everything you could mention. Everything. Yeah, it seemed like I got, that wouldn't be happening.
They don't have no respect. They'd be hiding underneath the house. That time I got to holler at them and get a whip necker, they start to question, man.
Yeah, but a long time ago it just didn't happen.

No. That's... I could tell your child or his child, go ahead and don't do that. Mm-hmm. Boy, he ain't gonna say nothing, see. Yes sir, yes ma'am, you know what I mean? He's going about his business. But then the family... Them now, they're ready to fight you.
That's right. The family gave out the family's permission to spank the children. Mm-hmm. And when they get home, they get another one.

Yeah. Yeah, a double one. Jump down there, whip you to self. And you better not go home and tell your parents. You're gonna tell them to get another one. Yeah, get another one. That's our last time for the reason.
That's right. Oh, boy. You get home, you can't go out and play. You get champion again. Boy, another gang coming up now, they're too free.
They're too free. Yeah, oh. Boy, I don't know.
